Grammar Point: A うが B うが (A uga B uga)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'no matter how...or', 'even if...or'.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + うが + Verb-volition form + うが
Example (Japanese): 朝早く起きるうが、夜遅く起きるうが、いつもバスが遅れる。
Example (Romaji): Asa hayaku okiru u ga, yoru osoku okiru u ga, itsumo basu ga okureru.
Example (English): No matter whether I wake up early in the morning or late at night, the bus is always late.

Grammar Point: A うと B うと (A uto B uto)
Meaning: To show both conditions A and B are equivalent or indifferent; 'whether A or B'.
Formation: い-adjective + うと, な-adjective + であろうと, Noun + であろうと
Example (Japanese): 雨が降ろうと晴れようと、私は毎日ジョギングをします。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga furo u to hare yo u to, watashi wa mainichi jogingu wo shimasu.
Example (English): Whether it's raining or sunny, I jog every day.

Grammar Point: A かたわら B (A katawara B)
Meaning: Expresses 'while also'; 'at the same time as'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + かたわら, Noun + のかたわら
Example (Japanese): 彼は仕事をするかたわら、大学に通っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shigoto o suru katawara, daigaku ni kayotte iru.
Example (English): While also working, he is attending university.

Grammar Point: A かれ B かれ (A kare B kare)
Meaning: Express either A or B or both; 'whether A or B'
Formation: Noun + かれ + Noun + かれ
Example (Japanese): 冬かれ夏かれ、毎日ジョギングする。
Example (Romaji): Fuyu kare natsu kare, mainichi jyogingu suru.
Example (English): Whether it is winter or summer, I jog every day.

Grammar Point: A だの B だの (A dano B dano)
Meaning: Used to list examples; 'things like', 'and so on'.
Formation: Noun + だの Noun + だの
Example (Japanese): 彼はいつも遅刻だの、仕事を忘れるだので困る。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa itsumo chikoku dano, shigoto wo wasureru dano de komaru.
Example (English): I'm troubled by him always being late, forgetting work, and so on.

Grammar Point: A であれ B であれ (A deare B deare)
Meaning: Used to indicate that something applies to multiple situations; 'whether A or B'.
Formation: Noun A + であれ + Noun B + であれ
Example (Japanese): 雨であれ雪であれ、試合は中止にならない。
Example (Romaji): Ame deare yuki deare, shiai wa chuushi ni naranai.
Example (English): Whether it's rain or snow, the match will not be cancelled.

Grammar Point: A というか B というか (A to iu ka B to iu ka)
Meaning: This phrase translates to 'rather than say A, it's more like B' or 'whether to call it A or B'.
Formation: Phrase A + というか, + Phrase B + というか
Example (Japanese): 彼は無礼というか、直接的というか、とにかく彼の言葉はすごくはっきりとしてます。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa burei to iu ka, chokusetsuteki to iu ka, tonikaku kare no kotoba wa sugoku hakkiri to shiteimasu.
Example (English): He is, rather than rude, more like direct; anyway, his words are very clear.

Grammar Point: A とも B とも (A tomo B tomo)
Meaning: Express two possibilities; 'either A or B', 'whether A or B'.
Formation: Noun + とも + Noun + とも
Example (Japanese): 決断とも誤りとも、結果は時間が教えてくれるでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Ketsudan tomo ayamari tomo, kekka wa jikan ga oshiete kureru deshou.
Example (English): Whether it's a decision or a mistake, time will tell the result.

Grammar Point: A にしろ B にしろ (A nishiro B nishiro)
Meaning: Whether it is A or B; Regardless of A or B
Formation: Noun A + にしろ + Noun B + にしろ, Verb-casual A + にしろ + Verb-casual B + にしろ
Example (Japanese): 暑いにしろ、寒いにしろ、毎日運動するべきです。
Example (Romaji): Atsui ni shiro, samui ni shiro, mainichi undou suru beki desu.
Example (English): Whether it's hot or cold, you should exercise every day.

Grammar Point: A にせよ B にせよ (A ni seyo B ni seyo)
Meaning: Either A or B, Regardless of A or B.
Formation: Noun + にせよ Noun + にせよ
Example (Japanese): 雨にせよ雪にせよ、試合は中止しない。
Example (Romaji): Ame ni seyo yuki ni seyo, shiai wa chuushi shinai.
Example (English): Whether it's rain or snow, the match won't be cancelled.

Grammar Point: A につけ B につけ （A ni tsuke B ni tsuke）
Meaning: Used to express 'whether... or...', 'both... and...', 'in either case'.
Formation: Phrase A + につけ、Phrase B + につけ
Example (Japanese): 彼には笑うにつけ泣くにつけ、とても魅力的な人だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni wa warau ni tsuke naku ni tsuke, totemo miryokuteki na hito da.
Example (English): He is very attractive whether he is laughing or crying.

Grammar Point: A のやら B のやら (A noyara B noyara)
Meaning: Used when the speaker is confused or unsure about multiple things.
Formation: Noun 1 + のやら + Noun 2 + のやら
Example (Japanese): 彼が怒っているのやら、悲しいのやら、私には分からない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga okotte iru no yara, kanashii no yara, watashi ni wa wakaranai.
Example (English): I don't know whether he is angry or sad.

Grammar Point: Noun1 が Noun1 なら、 Noun2 も Noun2 だ (A ga A nara, B mo B da)
Meaning: Indicates 'if Noun1 is the case then it is only natural that Noun2 is the case as well.'
Formation: Noun1 + が + Repeat Noun1 + なら、 + Noun2 + も + Repeat Noun2 + だ
Example (Japanese): 鬼が鬼なら、人間も人間だ。
Example (Romaji): Oni ga oni nara, ningen mo ningen da.
Example (English): If demons are demons, humans are also humans.

Grammar Point: Noun1 も Noun1 なら、Noun2 も Noun2 だ (A mo A nara, B mo B da)
Meaning: The structure expresses 'if it is said that ~, then it can be said that ~' or '~ not only, but also ~'.
Formation: Noun1 + も + Noun1 + なら、Noun2 + も + Noun2 + だ
Example (Japanese): 君も君なら、私も私だ。
Example (Romaji): Kimi mo kimi nara, watashi mo watashi da.
Example (English): If you are you, then I am also me.

Grammar Point: Noun + あっての + Noun (A atteno B)
Meaning: Expresses the idea 'nothing without'; something being indispensable for the existence of something else.
Formation: Noun1 + あっての + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 家族あっての私です。
Example (Romaji): Kazoku atte no watashi desu.
Example (English): I am nothing without my family.

Grammar Point: Noun かたがた (Noun kata gata)
Meaning: Used when doing one thing while also doing another; 'while', 'and at the same time'.
Formation: Noun + かたがた
Example (Japanese): 東京へ出張のかたがた、友人に会いに行った。
Example (Romaji): Toukyou e shuccho no kata gata, yujin ni ai ni itta.
Example (English): While I was on a business trip to Tokyo, I went to see a friend.

Grammar Point: Noun がてら (Noun gatera)
Meaning: At the same time; on the occasion of; while; along with.
Formation: Noun + がてら
Example (Japanese): 散歩がてらに、近くの公園で花を摘みました。
Example (Romaji): Sanpo gatera ni, chikaku no kouen de hana wo tsumimashita.
Example (English): While taking a walk, I picked flowers in the nearby park.

Grammar Point: Noun からある (〜kara aru)
Meaning: Expresses 'beginning from', 'from' or 'after'. Often used to indicate a high number or large scale.
Formation: Number + Counter + からある
Example (Japanese): 彼のコレクションは500個からある。
Example (Romaji): Kare no korekushon wa gohyaku ko kara aru.
Example (English): His collection starts from 500 items.

Grammar Point: Noun からする (Noun kara suru)
Meaning: Used to indicate that something is judged, estimated, or considered from a certain point or aspect.
Formation: Noun + からする
Example (Japanese): 彼の態度からすると、彼はその計画に反対しているようだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no taido kara suru to, kare wa sono keikaku ni hantai shiteiru you da.
Example (English): Judging from his attitude, he seems to be against the plan.

Grammar Point: Noun からの (~kara no)
Meaning: Defines the starting point or the origin; 'from'.
Formation: Noun + からの
Example (Japanese): 日本からの手紙を受け取りました。
Example (Romaji): Nihon kara no tegami wo uketorimashita.
Example (English): I received a letter from Japan.

Grammar Point: Noun から言わせれば (~kara iwasereba)
Meaning: Express the perspective of noun; 'from ~ point of view'
Formation: Noun + から言わせれば
Example (Japanese): 先生から言わせれば、毎日勉強するべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Sensei kara iwasereba, mainichi benkyou suru beki da.
Example (English): From the teacher's point of view, you should study every day.

Grammar Point: Noun + ぐるみ (〜gurumi)
Meaning: This term is used to describe 'entirely', 'altogether', 'as a whole' or 'collectively'.
Formation: Noun + ぐるみ
Example (Japanese): 家族ぐるみで旅行に行きました。
Example (Romaji): Kazoku gurumi de ryokou ni ikimashita.
Example (English): We went on a trip as a whole family.

Grammar Point: Noun こそあれ (~kosoare)
Meaning: Expresses the meaning 'even if'; 'no matter'.
Formation: Noun + こそあれ
Example (Japanese): 結果こそあれ、努力したことには変わりない。
Example (Romaji): Kekka koso are, doryoku shita koto ni wa kawari nai.
Example (English): Even if the result is what it is, the fact that we made an effort won't change.

Grammar Point: Noun こそ～が (~koso~ga)
Meaning: Used to emphasize that it is precisely because of something, that another statement is true.
Formation: Noun + こそ + Sentence + が
Example (Japanese): 初めてこそたいせつだが、諦めないことが一番大切だ。
Example (Romaji): Hajimete koso taisetsu da ga, akiramenai koto ga ichiban taisetsu da.
Example (English): The first step is important, of course, but what's most crucial is that you don't give up.

Grammar Point: Noun こそすれ (~koso sure)
Meaning: An emphatic expression for 'if anything', 'especially', and 'it is', which shows that other alternatives are hardly conceivable.
Formation: Noun + こそすれ
Example (Japanese): 仕事こそすれ何もしていない。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto kososure nani mo shite inai.
Example (English): I am not doing anything if not working.

Grammar Point: Noun ごとき / Noun ごとく (〜gotoki/〜gotoku)
Meaning: 'Like a...', 'like...', or 'as if'. Expresses similarity or metaphor.
Formation: Noun + ごとき, Noun + ごとく, Verb-casual + ごとく, い-Adjective + ごとく
Example (Japanese): 彼は天使のごとく純粋だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa tenshi no gotoku junsui da.
Example (English): He is pure like an angel.

Grammar Point: Noun じゃあるまいし (~ja aru mai shi)
Meaning: Expressing that something 'is not'; 'is not the case'.
Formation: Noun or Na-Adjective + じゃあるまいし
Example (Japanese): 彼は子供じゃあるまいし、その問題をしっかりと解決するべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kodomo ja aru mai shi, sono mondai o shikkari to kaiketsu suru beki da.
Example (English): He's not a child, he should solve that problem properly.

Grammar Point: Noun ずくめ (~zukume)
Meaning: Denotes 'entirely' or 'nothing but'.
Formation: Noun + ずくめ
Example (Japanese): 彼は最近、失敗ずくめだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa saikin, shippai zukume da.
Example (English): He has been nothing but failures recently.

Grammar Point: Noun だけではすまない (Noun dake dewa sumanai)
Meaning: Expresses 'not finish/end with just', 'cannot be settled only by'.
Formation: Noun + だけではすまない
Example (Japanese): この問題は謝罪だけではすまない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wa shazai dake dewa sumanai.
Example (English): This problem cannot be settled with just an apology.

Grammar Point: Noun たりとも～ない (~tari tomo ~nai)
Meaning: This expression shows the meaning of 'not even', 'not a single'.
Formation: Noun + たりとも + Negative Verb
Example (Japanese): 一分たりとも無駄にするな。
Example (Romaji): Ippun tari tomo muda ni suruna.
Example (English): Don't waste even a single minute.

Grammar Point: Noun たる Noun (~taru~)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'being in the condition or state of'
Formation: Noun1 + たる + Noun2
Example (Japanese): リーダータル者は、常に前を見て、他の人々を導くべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Riidaa taru mono wa, tsune ni mae o mite, hoka no hitobito o michibiku beki da.
Example (English): A person who is a leader should always look ahead and guide others.

Grammar Point: Noun ですら (~desura)
Meaning: Express 'even', 'even if', or 'as much as'.
Formation: Noun + ですら
Example (Japanese): 明日試験があるのに、彼はテキストブックを読むですらしない。
Example (Romaji): Ashita shiken ga aru noni, kare wa tekisutobukku o yomu desura shinai.
Example (English): Even though we have a test tomorrow, he doesn't even read the textbook.

Grammar Point: Noun でなくてなんだろう (〜de nakute nandarou)
Meaning: Expresses the speaker's strong belief that something is certainly the case.
Formation: Noun + でなくてなんだろう
Example (Japanese): これが真実でなくてなんだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kore ga shinjitsu de nakute nandarou.
Example (English): If this isn't the truth, then what is?

Grammar Point: Noun ではあるまいし (~dewa aru maishi)
Meaning: Use this phrase to mean 'it's not as if', 'it's not that'.
Formation: Noun + ではあるまいし
Example (Japanese): 彼女は、プロの歌手ではあるまいし、完璧を求めるな。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa, puro no kashu de wa arumai shi, kanpeki o motomeru na.
Example (English): She is not a professional singer, so don't demand perfection.

Grammar Point: Noun と Noun を兼ねて (Noun to Noun o kanete)
Meaning: Used to express the idea of doing two things at once or serving two purposes.
Formation: Noun + と + Noun + を兼ねて
Example (Japanese): お父さんは社長と経理部長を兼ねています。
Example (Romaji): Otousan wa shachou to keiri buchou o kanete imasu.
Example (English): My father serves as both the company president and the head of accounting.

Grammar Point: Noun といい Noun といい (〜toii〜toii)
Meaning: Used to express 'both A and B'; 'whether it's A or B'; 'not to mention A and also B'.
Formation: Noun1 + といい + Noun2 + といい + Comment
Example (Japanese): 日本の食べ物といい観光地といい、すべてが素晴らしいです。
Example (Romaji): Nihon no tabemono to ii kankouchi to ii, subete ga subarashii desu.
Example (English): Both Japanese food and tourist spots are all wonderful.

Grammar Point: Noun という Noun (~to iu~)
Meaning: Used to specify or define one noun with another; 'the noun called', 'the noun that is' or 'a certain'.
Formation: Noun1 という Noun2
Example (Japanese): 宮崎駿という人は有名なアニメーション監督です。
Example (Romaji): Miyazaki Hayao to iu hito wa yuumei na animation kantoku desu.
Example (English): The person called Hayao Miyazaki is a famous animation director.

Grammar Point: Noun というところだ (Noun to iu tokoro da)
Meaning: Means 'it's approximately...' or 'it's about...'. Used to show approximation or a general assessment.
Formation: Noun + というところだ
Example (Japanese): 今回の試験の合格者は半数というところだろう。
Example (Romaji): Konkai no shiken no goukakusha wa hansuu to iu tokoro darou.
Example (English): The passers in this exam would be approximately half.

Grammar Point: Noun + というもの (~ to iu mono)
Meaning: Used to express 'every', 'all'. Concept of generic reference.
Formation: Noun + というもの
Example (Japanese): 子供というものは、毎日たくさん遊びます。
Example (Romaji): Kodomo to iu mono wa, mainichi takusan asobimasu.
Example (English): Children, as a group, play a lot every day.

Grammar Point: Noun といったところだ (Noun to itta tokoro da)
Meaning: Expresses 'at most', 'as much as', 'limited to'.
Formation: Noun + といったところだ
Example (Japanese): 彼の英語レベルは初級といったところだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no eigo reberu wa shokyuu to itta tokoro da.
Example (English): His English level is at most beginner level.

Grammar Point: Noun といわず Noun といわず (A to iwazu B to iwazu)
Meaning: Expresses an idea of 'both A and B' or 'be it A or B'; 'not only A but also B'.
Formation: Noun1 + といわず + Noun2 + といわず + (rest of the sentence)
Example (Japanese): 冬といわず夏といわず、彼はいつもアイスクリームを食べます。
Example (Romaji): Fuyu to iwazu natsu to iwazu, kare wa itsumo aisukurīmu o tabemasu.
Example (English): Be it winter or summer, he always eats ice cream.

Grammar Point: Noun + ときたら (〜tokitara)
Meaning: Expresses strong feelings about a matter; 'speaking of', 'when it comes to'.
Formation: Noun + ときたら
Example (Japanese): 寿司ときたら、彼は何も食べれない。
Example (Romaji): Sushi tokitara, kare wa nani mo taberenai.
Example (English): When it comes to sushi, he can't eat anything.

Grammar Point: Noun とは比べものにならない (~to wa kurabemono ni naranai)
Meaning: To indicate something is not comparable with; 'not comparable to', 'beyond comparison'.
Formation: Noun + とは比べものにならない
Example (Japanese): 新しい車の速さは古い車とは比べ物にならない。
Example (Romaji): Atarashii kuruma no hayasa wa furui kuruma to wa kurabemono ni naranai.
Example (English): The speed of the new car is not comparable to the old car.

Grammar Point: Noun + ともあろう + Noun (~tomoarou~)
Meaning: Used to point out unbecoming behavior of a person or thing with certain status
Formation: Noun + ともあろう
Example (Japanese): 先生ともあろう者が、そんな間違いをするなんて。
Example (Romaji): Sensei tomoarou mono ga, sonna machigai o suru nante.
Example (English): For someone claiming to be a teacher, it's shocking that they would make such a mistake.

Grammar Point: Noun ともなると (〜to mo naruto)
Meaning: 'When it comes to..', 'In case of..', signifies change.
Formation: Noun + ともなると
Example (Japanese): クリスマスともなると、街中がきらきらと輝いて見えます。
Example (Romaji): Kurisumasu to mo naruto, machijuu ga kirakira to kagayaite miemasu.
Example (English): When it comes to Christmas, the whole city seems to sparkle.

Grammar Point: Noun ともなれば (〜to mo nareba)
Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'if it comes to', 'when', or 'once'.
Formation: Noun + ともなれば
Example (Japanese): 試験ともなれば、大抵の人が緊張するものです。
Example (Romaji): Shiken to mo nareba, taitei no hito ga kinchou suru mono desu.
Example (English): When it comes to exams, most people get nervous.

Grammar Point: Noun と相まって (~ to aimatte)
Meaning: Used to express 'in combination with', 'together with', 'along with'.
Formation: Noun + と相まって
Example (Japanese): 天気の良さと相まって、ピクニックは大成功でした。
Example (Romaji): Tenki no yosa to aimatte, pikunikku wa daiseikou deshita.
Example (English): Thanks to the good weather, the picnic was a great success.

Grammar Point: Noun なくして～はない (Noun nakushite ~ wa nai)
Meaning: Expresses the idea 'without ~, there can't be ~'; 'can't do ~ without first doing ~'.
Formation: Noun + なくして + Sentence ～はない
Example (Japanese): 努力なくして成功はない。
Example (Romaji): Doryoku nakushite seikou wa nai.
Example (English): There is no success without making an effort.

Grammar Point: Noun なしでは～ない (Noun nashi de wa ~nai)
Meaning: Expresses the necessity of something; 'cannot do without', 'not possible without'.
Formation: Noun + なしでは～ない
Example (Japanese): 水なしでは生きられない。
Example (Romaji): Mizu nashi de wa ikirarenai.
Example (English): We cannot live without water.

Grammar Point: Noun なしには～ない (Noun nashi ni wa ~nai)
Meaning: It means 'without', 'cannot do without', 'not possible without'.
Formation: Noun + なしには + Verb-negative
Example (Japanese): お金なしには生活ができない。
Example (Romaji): Okane nashi niwa seikatsu ga dekinai.
Example (English): Without money, life is not possible.

Grammar Point: Noun ならいざ知らず (~nara izashirazu)
Meaning: Expresses 'not to mention', 'let alone'.
Formation: Noun1 + ならいざ知らず + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 数学ならいざ知らず、物理なんて全然わからない。
Example (Romaji): Suugaku nara iza shirazu, butsuri nante zenzen wakaranai.
Example (English): I don't understand physics at all, not to mention maths.

Grammar Point: Noun + ならでは (~nara de wa)
Meaning: Expresses 'only', 'characteristic of'.
Formation: Noun + ならでは
Example (Japanese): これは日本ならではの風景ですね。
Example (Romaji): Kore wa Nihon nara dewa no fuukei desu ne.
Example (English): This is a landscape characteristic of Japan, isn't it?

Grammar Point: Noun なり Noun なり (A nari B nari)
Meaning: Indicates several alternatives; 'either...or', 'such as...'
Formation: Noun + なり + Noun + なり
Example (Japanese): 映画なり、音楽なり、何か趣味はありますか。
Example (Romaji): Eiga nari, ongaku nari, nanika shumi wa arimasu ka?
Example (English): Do you have any hobbies, like movies or music?

Grammar Point: Noun なりとも (~nari tomo)
Meaning: Indicates even a small amount or degree; 'even a little', 'at least'.
Formation: Noun + なりとも
Example (Japanese): 時間が限られているので、一時間なりとも練習すべきだ。
Example (Romaji): Jikan ga kagirarete iru node, ichi jikan nari tomo renshuu subeki da.
Example (English): Since time is limited, you should practice for at least an hour.

Grammar Point: Noun に Noun を重ねて (A ni B wo kasanete)
Meaning: This expression is used to describe repeated actions or states, 'one after another' or 'pile up'.
Formation: Noun に Noun を重ねて
Example (Japanese): 彼女は失敗に失敗を重ねて、とうとう会社を辞めた。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa shippai ni shippai wo kasanete, toutou kaisha wo yameta.
Example (English): She piled up failures upon failures and finally quit the company.

Grammar Point: Noun にあっては (Noun ni atte ha)
Meaning: Indicates a specific situation or environment in which something happens or is the case.
Formation: Noun + にあっては
Example (Japanese): 戦争時にあっては、すべての人々が困難に直面していました。
Example (Romaji): Sensouji ni atte ha, subete no hito ga konnan ni chokumen shiteimashita.
Example (English): In wartime, all people were facing difficulties.

Grammar Point: Noun にあるまじき Noun (Noun ni aru majiki Noun)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'unfitting', 'unbecoming' or 'inappropriate'.
Formation: Noun1 にあるまじき Noun2
Example (Japanese): 彼は教師にあるまじき言動をとった。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kyoushi ni aru majiki gendou wo totta.
Example (English): He took actions that are unbecoming of a teacher.

Grammar Point: Noun にして (Noun ni shite)
Meaning: Expresses the idea 'even for', 'even though', or 'in spite of'.
Formation: Noun + にして
Example (Japanese): 彼は医者にしてその基本的な知識がないのが信じられない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa isha ni shite sono kihonteki na chishiki ga nai no ga shinjirarenai.
Example (English): I can't believe that even as a doctor, he doesn't have that basic knowledge.

Grammar Point: Noun にして初めて (Noun nishite hajimete)
Meaning: Expresses 'only when/after... for the first time'.
Formation: Noun + にして初めて
Example (Japanese): 大人にして初めて、親の苦労が分かった。
Example (Romaji): Otona ni shite hajimete, oya no kurou ga wakatta.
Example (English): Only when I became an adult, I understood my parents' struggles for the first time.

Grammar Point: Noun にすら (〜ni sura)
Meaning: Expresses the concept of 'even'; 'even in', 'even as', 'even to'.
Formation: Noun + にすら
Example (Japanese): 彼にすらその問題は解けなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni sura sono mondai wa tokenakatta.
Example (English): Even he could not solve that problem.

Grammar Point: Noun にとどまらず～も (~ ni todomarazu ~ mo)
Meaning: This expresses the idea of 'not only...but also', 'not stopping at...'
Formation: Noun + にとどまらず + Noun + も
Example (Japanese): このアプリは、日本語にとどまらず、他の言語もサポートしています。
Example (Romaji): Kono apuri wa, nihongo ni todomarazu, hoka no gengo mo sapooto shite imasu.
Example (English): This app not only supports Japanese, but also other languages.

Grammar Point: Noun にひきかえ Noun は (~ni hikikae ~ wa)
Meaning: Represents 'in contrast to', 'as opposed to'.
Formation: Noun 1 + にひきかえ + Noun 2 + は
Example (Japanese): 彼の親切さにひきかえ、彼女は無感情だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no shinsetsusa ni hikikae, kanojo wa mukanjou da.
Example (English): In contrast to his kindness, she is emotionless.

Grammar Point: Noun にもまして (〜ni mo mashite)
Meaning: This expresses 'Even more than; exceeding'.
Formation: Noun + にもまして
Example (Japanese): 私は彼にもまして、音楽を愛しています。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa kare ni mo mashite, ongaku o aishiteimasu.
Example (English): I love music even more than he does.

Grammar Point: Noun によらず (～ni yorazu)
Meaning: Regardless of, irrespective of.
Formation: Noun + によらず
Example (Japanese): 結果は勉強時間によらず変わらないでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Kekka wa benkyou jikan ni yorazu kawaranai deshou.
Example (English): The result will not change regardless of the study time.

Grammar Point: Noun に先駆けて (〜ni saki gakete)
Meaning: Meaning 'ahead of', 'before', or 'preceding in time'.
Formation: Noun + に先駆けて
Example (Japanese): この映画は日本に先駆けて、アメリカで公開されました。
Example (Romaji): Kono eiga wa Nippon ni saki gakete, Amerika de koukai saremashita.
Example (English): This film was released in America ahead of Japan.

Grammar Point: Noun に即した Noun (A ni sokushita B)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'in accordance with', 'based on'.
Formation: Noun1 + に即した + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 社会のニーズに即した教育改革が必要だ。
Example (Romaji): shakai no nīzu ni sokushita kyouiku kaikaku ga hitsuyou da.
Example (English): We need an educational reform that is in accordance with the needs of society.

Grammar Point: Noun に即して Verb (〜ni soku shite ~)
Meaning: The grammar point Noun に即して Verb is used to mean 'to act in accordance with', 'in line with' or 'based on'.
Formation: Noun + に即して + Verb
Example (Japanese): 会社のポリシーに即して行動しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kaisha no porishi ni soku shite koudo shimashou.
Example (English): Let's act in accordance with the company's policy.

Grammar Point: Noun に言わせれば (Noun ni iwasereba)
Meaning: Expresses 'according to', 'if you ask', 'in the opinion of'.
Formation: Noun + に言わせれば
Example (Japanese): 先生に言わせれば、毎日勉強することが重要だと言う。
Example (Romaji): Sensei ni iwasereba, mainichi benkyou suru koto ga juuyou da to iu.
Example (English): According to the teacher, it's important to study every day.

Grammar Point: Noun に限ったことではない (〜ni kagitta koto dewa nai)
Meaning: Indicates that something is not only limited to; 'not only', 'not just'.
Formation: Noun + に限ったことではない
Example (Japanese): この問題は日本に限ったことではない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wa Nihon ni kagitta koto dewa nai.
Example (English): This issue is not only limited to Japan.

Grammar Point: Noun に限ったことでもない (~ ni kagitta koto demo nai)
Meaning: 'Not limited to'; 'not just', 'not exclusively'.
Formation: Noun + に限ったことでもない
Example (Japanese): この試験が難しいのは、数学に限ったことでもない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shiken ga muzukashii no wa, suugaku ni kagitta koto demo nai.
Example (English): The exam being difficult is not limited to just math.

Grammar Point: Noun に限る (~ni kagiru)
Meaning: Expresses the idea that 'nothing but', 'nothing is better than'.
Formation: Noun + に限る
Example (Japanese): こういう時には家族に話すに限る。
Example (Romaji): Kou iu toki ni wa kazoku ni hanasu ni kagiru.
Example (English): At times like this, there's nothing better than talking to your family.

Grammar Point: Noun ぬいた Noun (A nuita B)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'taking something out from something else'.
Formation: Noun1 + をぬいた + Noun2
Example (Japanese): このサラダはにんじんをぬいたサラダです。
Example (Romaji): Kono sarada wa ninjin o nuita sarada desu.
Example (English): This is a salad with the carrots removed.

Grammar Point: Noun + ぬいて（~nuite)
Meaning: This is a way to express 'minus' or 'except for' some specific noun.
Formation: Noun + ぬいて
Example (Japanese): 私たちは、彼ぬいて全員が集まることができました。
Example (Romaji): Watashitachi wa, kare nuite zen'in ga atsumaru koto ga dekimashita.
Example (English): We were able to gather everyone except for him.

Grammar Point: ～ぬく (~nuku)
Meaning: Expresses the concept of doing something completely or thoroughly.
Formation: Verb-stem + ぬく
Example (Japanese): 彼は一日中本を読みぬく。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa ichinichijuu hon o yominuku.
Example (English): He will read the book all day long.

Grammar Point: Noun+のいかんだ (Noun no ikan da)
Meaning: Depends on; up to
Formation: Noun + のいかんだ/Noun + のいかんでは
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るのいかんで決めよう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru no ikan de kimeyou.
Example (English): Let's decide depending on whether he comes or not.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんでは (Noun no ikan de wa)
Meaning: It depends on the Noun
Formation: Noun + のいかんでは
Example (Japanese): 試験の結果のいかんでは、大学の入学許可を得られるかどうかが決まります。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no kekka no ikan dewa, daigaku no nyuugaku kyoka o erareru ka douka ga kimarimasu.
Example (English): Whether you can get permission to enter university depends on the result of the exam.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんにかかわらず (Noun no ikan ni kakawarazu)
Meaning: Regardless of, irrespective of.
Formation: Noun + のいかんにかかわらず
Example (Japanese): 結果のいかんにかかわらず、彼は決定を後悔しなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kekka no ikan ni kakawarazu, kare wa kettei wo koukai shinakatta.
Example (English): Regardless of the outcome, he didn't regret his decision.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんによっては (Noun no ikan ni yotte wa)
Meaning: Depending on the matter; depending on noun
Formation: Noun + のいかんによっては
Example (Japanese): 天気のいかんによっては、ピクニックを延期しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Tenki no ikan ni yotte wa, pikunikku o enki shimashou.
Example (English): Depending on the weather, we should postpone the picnic.

Grammar Point: Noun のいかんによらず (~ no ikan ni yorazu)
Meaning: Means 'regardless of', 'irrespective of', or 'no matter'
Formation: Noun + のいかんによらず
Example (Japanese): 試験の結果のいかんによらず、自分を信じ続けてください。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no kekka no ikan ni yorazu, jibun o shinji tsudzukete kudasai.
Example (English): Regardless of the test results, keep believing in yourself.

Grammar Point: Noun のごとき Noun (A no gotoki B)
Meaning: Expresses 'like' or 'as if'; something/someone resembles much to something else
Formation: Noun1 + のごとき + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 彼は神のごとき存在だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kami no gotoki sonzai da.
Example (English): He is an existence like a god.

Grammar Point: Noun のことだから (〜no koto dakara)
Meaning: Because it is about ~, considering it's ~
Formation: Noun + のことだから
Example (Japanese): 彼のことだから、きっと大丈夫だと思う。
Example (Romaji): Kare no koto dakara, kitto daijoubu da to omou.
Example (English): Because it's him, I think it will certainly be fine.

Grammar Point: Noun の 嫌いがある (Noun no kirai ga aru)
Meaning: Have a dislike for a particular Noun
Formation: Noun + の嫌いがある
Example (Japanese): 彼は魚の嫌いがあるので、寿司を食べません。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sakana no kirai ga aru node, sushi o tabemasen.
Example (English): He has a dislike for fish, so he doesn't eat sushi.

Grammar Point: Noun の手前 (~no temae)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'Before doing action; on the verge of'.
Formation: Noun + の手前
Example (Japanese): 試験の手前、遊びに行くのは止めた方がいい
Example (Romaji): Shiken no temae, asobi ni iku no wa yameta hou ga ii.
Example (English): Just before the exam, it's better to stop going to play.

Grammar Point: Noun の極み (〜no kiwami)
Meaning: Used to express the extreme or utmost point of something.
Formation: Noun + の極み
Example (Japanese): 彼の料理の極みは、誰もマネできない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no ryouri no kiwami wa, daremo mane dekinai.
Example (English): The pinnacle of his cooking, nobody can imitate.

Grammar Point: Noun の 至り (~no itari)
Meaning: Expresses the highest degree of something, 'the height of', 'the extreme of'.
Formation: Noun + の至り
Example (Japanese): 彼の冗談には驚きの至りだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no joudan ni wa odoroki no itari da.
Example (English): His jokes are the height of surprise.

Grammar Point: Noun はいざ知らず (~ wa iza shirazu)
Meaning: Used to express that it's understood why 'A' would be the case but not 'B'. It's like saying 'Well, I can understand it for A, but for B...?'
Formation: Noun + はいざ知らず, Noun + だけど/しかし/とは言え
Example (Japanese): 彼が遅れるのはいざ知らず、彼女まで遅刻するとは意外だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga okureru no wa iza shirazu, kanojo made chikoku suru towa igai da.
Example (English): Well, I can understand him being late, but even her...? That's surprising.

Grammar Point: Noun は おろか～すら (Noun wa oroka ～sura)
Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'not to mention ~, even ~'.
Formation: Noun1 はおろか, Noun2 すら/さえ
Example (Japanese): 彼は走るはおろか、速く歩くことすらできない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa hashiru wa oroka, hayaku aruku koto sura dekinai.
Example (English): He can't even walk fast, let alone run.

Grammar Point: Noun はおろか～まで (~wa oroka ~made)
Meaning: Even; not to mention; let alone
Formation: Noun1 + はおろか + Noun2 + まで
Example (Japanese): 彼は英語はおろか、日本語までペラペラなんです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa eigo wa oroka, nihongo made perapera nan desu.
Example (English): He is not just fluent in English, but even in Japanese.

Grammar Point: Noun はおろか～も (Noun wa oroka ～ mo)
Meaning: 'Not only...but also', 'not to mention', 'to say nothing of'
Formation: Noun + はおろか + Noun + も
Example (Japanese): 絵を描くことはおろか、字さえ書けない。
Example (Romaji): E wo kaku koto wa oroka, ji sae kakenai.
Example (English): He can't even write, let alone draw.

Grammar Point: Noun はさておき (~ wa sateoki)
Meaning: Means 'putting aside', 'aside from', 'notwithstanding'.
Formation: Noun + はさておき
Example (Japanese): 試験の結果はさておき、この学期はとても学ぶことが多かった。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no kekka wa sateoki, kono gakki wa totemo manabu koto ga ookatta.
Example (English): Aside from the exam results, I learned a lot this semester.

Grammar Point: Noun + はどうであれ (~ wa dou de are)
Meaning: This phrase means 'regardless of' or 'no matter how…'. It is used to express the idea that 'whatever the state or condition of the noun, we should not care'.
Formation: Noun + はどうであれ
Example (Japanese): 天候はどうであれ、試合は行われます。
Example (Romaji): Tenkou wa dou de are, shiai wa okonawaremasu.
Example (English): No matter what the weather is, the match will be held.

Grammar Point: Noun まみれ (~mamire)
Meaning: Used to express a state in which something is entirely covered, smeared, or filled with something else.
Formation: Noun + まみれ
Example (Japanese): 彼は泥まみれになって帰ってきた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa doro mamire ni natte kaette kita.
Example (English): He returned home covered in mud.

Grammar Point: Noun もさることながら Noun も (A mo saru koto nagara B mo)
Meaning: Meaning 'not only... but also'. Expresses that both Nouns are true or notable, but the second is particularly emphasized.
Formation: Noun1 + もさることながら + Noun2 + も
Example (Japanese): 彼の歌唱力もさることながら、ダンスも素晴らしい。
Example (Romaji): Kare no kashou-ryoku mo saru koto nagara, dansu mo subarashii.
Example (English): Not only his singing ability but also his dancing is wonderful.

Grammar Point: Noun も兼ねて (~mo kane te)
Meaning: Used to express 'as well as', 'also', 'at the same time'.
Formation: Noun + も兼ねて
Example (Japanese): 散歩も兼ねて、公園に行きました。
Example (Romaji): Sanpo mo kanete, kouen ni ikimashita.
Example (English): I went to the park, also for a walk.

Grammar Point: Noun も相まって (~mo aimatte)
Meaning: Used to express that combined with something else, it caused a certain outcome
Formation: Noun + も相まって
Example (Japanese): 気候も相まって、この地域は農業に適しています。
Example (Romaji): Kikou mo aimatte, kono chiiki wa nougyou ni tekishiteimasu.
Example (English): Combined with the climate, this area is suitable for agriculture.

Grammar Point: Noun を おいて他に Verb ない (〜wo oite hoka ni〜nai)
Meaning: This grammar point means 'apart from ~ there's nothing else', implying the Noun is the best or most suitable choice.
Formation: Noun + をおいて他に + Verb negative form
Example (Japanese): この仕事を彼に任せる人をおいて他にいない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shigoto wo kare ni makaseru hito wo oite hoka ni inai.
Example (English): Apart from him, there's no one else to entrust this job to.

Grammar Point: Noun をもって (~wo motte)
Meaning: Used to indicate means, methods, or time; 'with', 'by means of', 'at'.
Formation: Noun + をもって
Example (Japanese): 彼は誠実さをもって人々に信頼されています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa seijitsusa wo motte hitobito ni shinrai sarete imasu.
Example (English): He is trusted by people with his honesty.

Grammar Point: Noun をものともせずに (Noun wo mono tomo sezu ni)
Meaning: Expresses the idea that 'despite something, action was carried out', simply translating to 'without being phased by something'.
Formation: Noun + をものともせずに
Example (Japanese): 彼女は怖さをものともせずに、暗闇の中へ進んで行った。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa kowasa wo mono tomo sezu ni, kurayami no naka e susunde itta.
Example (English): Despite her fear, she went ahead into the darkness.

Grammar Point: Noun をよそに (~wo yoso ni)
Meaning: Despite; Notwithstanding; Regardless of
Formation: Noun + をよそに
Example (Japanese): 経済危機をよそに、彼は高級な車を買った。
Example (Romaji): Keizai kiki wo yoso ni, kare wa koukyuu na kuruma wo katta.
Example (English): Despite the economic crisis, he bought a luxury car.

Grammar Point: Noun を余儀なくされる (Noun wo yogi naku sareru)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of being forced into a certain situation, 'to be compelled', 'to be obliged'.
Formation: Noun + を + 余儀なくされる
Example (Japanese): 彼は経済的困難により、退学を余儀なくされた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa keizai-teki konnan ni yori, taigaku wo yogi naku saremashita.
Example (English): Due to financial difficulties, he was forced to drop out of school.

Grammar Point: Noun を前提として (Noun wo zentei toshite)
Meaning: Use to express 'on the assumption of', 'based on'.
Formation: Noun + を前提として
Example (Japanese): 成功を前提として、ビジネスプランを作成しました。
Example (Romaji): Seikou wo zentei toshite, bijinesu puran wo sakusei shimashita.
Example (English): We made a business plan on the assumption of success.

Grammar Point: Noun を前提にして (Noun wo zentei ni shite)
Meaning: Assuming; presupposing; on the assumption of.
Formation: Noun + を前提にして
Example (Japanese): 好天を前提にして、明日のピクニックの計画を立てました。
Example (Romaji): Kouten wo zentei ni shite, ashita no pikunikku no keikaku wo tatemashita.
Example (English): We planned tomorrow's picnic assuming fine weather.

Grammar Point: Noun を境にして (Noun wo sakai ni shite)
Meaning: Means 'as a turning point of'; 'since (time)'; 'from (time) on'
Formation: Noun + を境に(して)
Example (Japanese): 父の死を境にして、彼の性格が一変した。
Example (Romaji): Chichi no shi wo sakai ni shite, kare no seikaku ga ippen shita.
Example (English): His personality changed completely since his father's death.

Grammar Point: Noun を機にして (~wo ki ni shite)
Meaning: To take the opportunity to, taking the occasion to, on the occasion of.
Formation: Noun + を機にして
Example (Japanese): 引っ越しを機にして、家具を新しくしました。
Example (Romaji): Hikkoshi wo ki ni shite, kagu wo atarashiku shimashita
Example (English): I took the opportunity of moving to get new furniture.

Grammar Point: Noun を皮切りに / を皮切りにして (Noun wo kakikiri ni / wo kawakiri ni shite)
Meaning: Used to indicate the starting point of some series of events or actions; 'starting with', 'beginning with'.
Formation: Noun + を皮切りに / を皮切りにして
Example (Japanese): 彼はその論文を皮切りにして複数の研究を開始した。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sono ronbun wo kakikiri ni shite fukusu no kenkyu wo kaishi shita.
Example (English): Starting with that thesis, he started multiple research projects.

Grammar Point: Noun を皮切りにして (Noun wo kawakiri ni shite)
Meaning: Used to express 'Starting with', 'Beginning with'
Formation: Noun + を皮切りに (して)
Example (Japanese): 彼はその日を皮切りにして毎日ジムに通い始めました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sono hi wo kawakiri ni shite mainichi gym ni kayoi hajimemashita.
Example (English): Starting from that day, he began to go to the gym every day.

Grammar Point: Noun を禁じ得ない (〜wo kinjienai)
Meaning: 'Cannot help but do', or 'inevitable'
Formation: Noun + を禁じ得ない
Example (Japanese): この結果には驚きを禁じ得ない。
Example (Romaji): Kono kekka ni wa odoroki wo kinjienai.
Example (English): I can't help but be surprised at this result.

Grammar Point: Noun を経て (〜wo hete)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'through' or 'via'; going through some process or phase.
Formation: Noun + を経て
Example (Japanese): 彼は苦労を経て成功を手に入れた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kurou wo hete seikou wo te ni ireta.
Example (English): He achieved success through hardships.

Grammar Point: Noun を踏まえて (〜wo fumaete)
Meaning: Based on; taking into account; in light of
Formation: Noun + を踏まえて
Example (Japanese): 過去の結果を踏まえて、新たな計画を立てました。
Example (Romaji): Kako no kekka wo fumaete, aratana keikaku wo tatemashita.
Example (English): Based on the previous results, we have made a new plan.

Grammar Point: Noun を限りに (Noun wo kagiri ni)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'as of', 'with' or 'from', indicating the end of something or a point of change.
Formation: Noun + を限りに
Example (Japanese): 今年度を限りに、この大学での教授活動を終えるつもりです。
Example (Romaji): Kotoshido wo kagiri ni, kono daigaku de no kyouju katsudou wo oeru tsumori desu.
Example (English): I intend to end my teaching activities at this university as of this academic year.

Grammar Point: Noun 並み (~nami)
Meaning: Indicates 'like' or 'as' something or someone; 'equivalent to', 'around'.
Formation: Noun + 並み
Example (Japanese): 彼はプロのボクサー並みの力を持っています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa puro no bokusa- nami no chikara o motte imasu.
Example (English): He has power equivalent to a professional boxer.

Grammar Point: Noun + 前提で（~zentei de)
Meaning: Expresses the condition or requirement for something to be established; 'on the assumption that', 'under the condition of'.
Formation: Noun + 前提で
Example (Japanese): 説明できる英語力がある前提で、この仕事を引き受けてください。
Example (Romaji): Setsumei dekiru eigo-ryoku ga aru zentei de, kono shigoto o hikiuketekudasai.
Example (English): Please accept this job on the assumption that you have English skills to explain.

Grammar Point: Noun 限りで (~ kagiri de)
Meaning: As long as; for the duration; while
Formation: Noun + 限りで
Example (Japanese): 私が生きている限りで、あなたを支えます。
Example (Romaji): Watashi ga ikite iru kagiri de, anata wo sasaemasu.
Example (English): As long as I'm alive, I will support you.

Grammar Point: Verb がてら (~ gatera)
Meaning: Expresses doing something while doing another; 'while', 'on the occasion of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + がてら
Example (Japanese): 散歩がてらに郵便局へ行った。
Example (Romaji): Sanpo gatera ni yuubinkyoku e itta.
Example (English): I went to the post office while taking a walk.

Grammar Point: Verb こそすれ (~koso sure)
Meaning: Expresses 'the extent or degree of doing something is so much that...' or 'does enough to...'
Formation: Verb-ます stem + こそすれ
Example (Japanese): 彼は友達を助けることこそすれ、自分を卑下することはありません。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa tomodachi o tasukeru koto koso sure, jibun o hika suru koto wa arimasen.
Example (English): He does enough to help his friends but he never belittles himself.

Grammar Point: Verb させられる (~saserareru)
Meaning: Expresses 'being forced to do something' or 'being made to do something'.
Formation: Verb-casual(non-past)+させられる
Example (Japanese): 彼に無理やり飲ませられた。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni muriyari nomasaserareta.
Example (English): He forced me to drink against my will.

Grammar Point: Verb ざるを得ない (~ zaru wo enai)
Meaning: 'Cannot but', 'have no choice but to', 'forced to'
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ざるを得ない
Example (Japanese): この仕事が嫌ならもう辞めざるを得ない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shigoto ga iya nara mou yamezaru o enai.
Example (English): If you hate this job, you have no choice but to quit.

Grammar Point: Verb ずじまい (~zu jimai)
Meaning: Expressing regret for not having done something; not being able to; not having the chance to.
Formation: Verb-ない form (remove ない） + ずじまい
Example (Japanese): 日本へ来て、一度も富士山を見ることなく帰国せずじまいだ。
Example (Romaji): Nihon e kite, ichido mo Fuji-san o miru koto naku kikoku sezu jimai da.
Example (English): I came to Japan but ended up going home without ever getting to see Mt. Fuji.

Grammar Point: Verb ずとも (〜zu tomo)
Meaning: This structure is used to mean 'Even without doing (an action), (an action) is still achievable'.
Formation: Verb-negative stem + ずとも
Example (Japanese): 朝ごはんを食べずとも、働くことができます。
Example (Romaji): Asagohan wo tabezu tomo, hataraku koto ga dekimasu.
Example (English): Even without eating breakfast, I can work.

Grammar Point: Verb ずにはおかない (~zuni wa okanai)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'cannot help but...', 'cannot leave it as it is' or 'must do something'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ずにはおかない
Example (Japanese): 彼が困っていると聞いたら、助けずにはおかない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga komatte iru to kitta, tasukezuni wa okanai.
Example (English): If I hear that he is in trouble, I cannot help but assist him.

Grammar Point: Verb ずにはすまない (Verb zuni wa sumanai)
Meaning: 'Cannot do without', 'have to', 'unavoidable'.
Formation: Verb-ないform(remove ない) + ずにはすまない
Example (Japanese): この問題を解決しないと、社会全体が影響を受けるので、解決せずにはすまない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai o kaiketsu shinauto, shakai zentai ga eikyou o ukeru node, kaiketsu sezu niwa sumanai.
Example (English): Since this issue will affect the entire society if not resolved, we cannot do without resolving it.

Grammar Point: Verb そうにない (Verb sou ni nai)
Meaning: Expresses unlikelihood or that something is not likely to happen.
Formation: Verb-stem + そうにない
Example (Japanese): 彼はそんなに早く走るそうにない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sonna ni hayaku hashiru sou ni nai.
Example (English): He doesn't seem likely to run that fast.

Grammar Point: Verb そうもない (〜sou monai)
Meaning: Expresses the negative potential; 'it doesn't seem like', 'it's not likely'.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + そうもない
Example (Japanese): 今日中に仕事を終えるそうもない。
Example (Romaji): Kyoujuu ni shigoto o oeru sou monai.
Example (English): It doesn't seem like I'll finish the work today.

Grammar Point: Verb そばから (〜soba kara)
Meaning: Expresses the notion that as soon as one action finishes, another begins.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + そばから
Example (Japanese): 掃除をするそばから子供たちが散らかす。
Example (Romaji): Souji wo suru soba kara kodomo-tachi ga chirakasu.
Example (English): As soon as I clean, the kids mess it up.

Grammar Point: Verb たが最後 (〜ta ga saigo)
Meaning: Expression used to denote the idea that 'once something has occurred, it is final'; 'once', 'as soon as', 'the moment'.
Formation: Verb-casual, past (た form) + が最後
Example (Japanese): 彼が一度怒ったが最後、誰も彼を止めることはできません。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga ichido okotta ga saigo, dare mo kare o tomeru koto wa dekimasen.
Example (English): Once he gets angry, no one can stop him.

Grammar Point: Verb たことにしてください (~ ta koto ni shite kudasai)
Meaning: Asking someone to pretend or accept that something has already happened or taken a certain state.
Formation: Verb(past, casual) + ことにしてください
Example (Japanese): 昨日のことは忘れたことにしてください。
Example (Romaji): Kinou no koto wa wasureta koto ni shite kudasai.
Example (English): Please act as if you have forgotten about yesterday.

Grammar Point: Verb たら Verb たで (~ tara ~ tade)
Meaning: Expresses the sequence of actions; 'after doing..., did...'.
Formation: Verb(たform) + ら + Verb(たform) + で
Example (Japanese): 彼と話したら、思ってたのと全然違う人だったで。
Example (Romaji): Kare to hanashitara, omotteta no to zenzen chigau hito datta de.
Example (English): After talking to him, he was different from the person I had thought.

Grammar Point: Verb たら きりがない (Verb tara kiri ga nai)
Meaning: Represents an endless cycle of doing something; 'if one starts doing something, it will not stop'
Formation: Verb-た form + きりがない
Example (Japanese): このエンジンを修理すれば、また壊れて、また修理すれば、きりがない。
Example (Romaji): Kono enjin o shuuri sureba, mata kowarete, mata shuuri sureba, kiri ga nai.
Example (English): If I fix this engine and then it breaks again and I fix it again, it will never end.

Grammar Point: Verb たら最後 (〜tara saigo)
Meaning: Expresses that once a certain action happens, a situation changes irreversibly; 'once', 'after'.
Formation: Verb-た form + 最後
Example (Japanese): このゲームを始めたら最後、時間の経つのを忘れてしまいます。
Example (Romaji): Kono geemu wo hajimetara saigo, jikan no tatsu no wo wasurete shimaimasu.
Example (English): Once you start this game, you lose track of time.

Grammar Point: Verb つ Verb つ (Verb tsu Verb tsu)
Meaning: Expresses a series of actions happening repeatedly one after another.
Formation: Verb-stem(masu-form) + つ  + same Verb-stem(masu-form) + つ
Example (Japanese): 朝から晩まで働きつ勉強つで疲れてしまった。
Example (Romaji): Asa kara ban made hataraki tsu benkyou tsu de tsukarete shimatta.
Example (English): I'm exhausted from working and studying from morning till night.

Grammar Point: Verb てからというもの (Verb te kara to iu mono)
Meaning: Expresses a change that has been consistent since a certain time or event.
Formation: Verb-てform + からというもの
Example (Japanese): 彼女と別れてからというもの、一人で過ごす時間が増えました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo to wakarete kara toiu mono, hitori de sugosu jikan ga fuetamashita.
Example (English): Since breaking up with her, the time I spend alone has increased.

Grammar Point: Verb てこそ (Verb te koso)
Meaning: Express the idea that 'only by doing something, something else can be achieved or realized.'
Formation: Verb-て form + こそ
Example (Japanese): 実際に使ってこそ、その価値を理解できる。
Example (Romaji): Jissai ni tsukatte koso, sono kachi wo rikai dekiru.
Example (English): You can understand its value only by actually using it.

Grammar Point: Verb ては (～te wa)
Meaning: Expresses a repeated negative event; 'whenever', 'the more...the more'.
Formation: Verb-てform + は
Example (Japanese): 彼女に会うたびに、私は緊張してしまいます。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ni au tabi ni, watashi wa kinchou shite shimaimasu.
Example (English): Whenever I meet her, I get nervous.

Grammar Point: Verb ては Verb (~ te wa ~)
Meaning: Used to express a repeated pattern of action, commonly translating into English as 'every time' or 'whenever'.
Formation: Verb-て form + は + Verb
Example (Japanese): 私が通勤しては、電子書籍を読んでいます。
Example (Romaji): Watashi ga tsuukin shite wa, denshi shoseki o yonde imasu.
Example (English): Whenever I commute, I read e-books.

Grammar Point: Verb てまでも (~ temademo)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'even if it means....'; 'no matter what it takes'
Formation: Verb-て form + までも
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格するために、寝る時間を削ってまでも勉強します。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku suru tame ni, neru jikan o kezutte mademo benkyou shimasu.
Example (English): In order to pass the exam, I will study even if it means cutting down on sleep.

Grammar Point: Verb てみせる (Verb te miseru)
Meaning: Expresses 'show by doing', 'demonstrate', 'prove by action'.
Formation: Verb-te form + みせる
Example (Japanese): 彼はそのパズルを解いてみせた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sono pazuru o toite miseta.
Example (English): He solved the puzzle to show me.

Grammar Point: Verb てやまない (Verb te yamanai)
Meaning: To express the idea of 'doing something incessantly', 'can't help but do'.
Formation: Verb-te form + やまない
Example (Japanese): 私は母を思ってやまない。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa haha o omotte yamanai.
Example (English): I can't help but think about my mother.

Grammar Point: Verb ないではおかない (~ nai de wa okanai)
Meaning: Used to indicate that something definitely happens as a result or a consequence of a certain action.
Formation: Verb-ない form + ではおかない
Example (Japanese): 彼女は毎回遅刻をしては、先生に怒られないではおかない。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa maikai chikoku o shite wa, sensei ni okorarenai dewa okanai.
Example (English): Every time she's late, she wouldn't fail to get scolded by the teacher.

Grammar Point: Verb ないではすまない (Verb nai dewa sumanai)
Meaning: Express a condition that 'cannot end without doing', 'must do no matter what', or 'cannot help but do'.
Formation: Verb-negative form + ではすまない
Example (Japanese): 失敗をしたら、謝らないではすまない。
Example (Romaji): Shippai o shitara, ayamaranai dewa sumanai.
Example (English): If you make a mistake, you cannot end without apologizing.

Grammar Point: Verb ないまでも (Verb nai made mo)
Meaning: Even if not completely; at least
Formation: Verb-ない form + までも
Example (Japanese): 全てを理解しないまでも、少なくとも基本的なことは分かればいい。
Example (Romaji): Subete wo rikai shinai made mo, sukunakutomo kihon tekina koto wa wakareba ii.
Example (English): Even if you don't understand everything, at least as long as you understand the basics.

Grammar Point: Verb ないものだろうか (Verb nai mono darou ka)
Meaning: Expressing the desire or inquisition; 'Can't I/you/we', 'Shouldn't I/you/we'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ないものだろうか
Example (Japanese): もっと時間があれば、ここに来るないものだろうか。
Example (Romaji): Motto jikan ga areba, koko ni kuru nai mono darou ka.
Example (English): If I had more time, wouldn't it be possible to come here?

Grammar Point: Verb ないものでもない (Verb nai mono demo nai)
Meaning: Expresses the idea that 'it's not that I don't...'; 'it's not that there aren't...'
Formation: Verb-negative form (ない form) + ものでもない
Example (Japanese): 旅行に行きたいと思うこともないものでもない。
Example (Romaji): Ryokou ni ikitai to omou koto mo nai mono demo nai.
Example (English): It's not that I don't ever want to travel.

Grammar Point: Verb の ない Noun (~ no nai ~)
Meaning: Used to modify a noun with a negative verb form; 'Noun where verb does not happen'.
Formation: Verb in negative form + の + Noun
Example (Japanese): 笑いのない人生は、つまらない。
Example (Romaji): Warai no nai jinsei wa, tsumaranai.
Example (English): A life without laughter is boring.

Grammar Point: Verb ば きり が ない (〜ba kiri ga nai)
Meaning: Used to indicate an absence of any limit or end, expressing 'if one starts to …, there will be no end to it'.
Formation: Verb-conditional form + ば + きりがない
Example (Japanese): 彼のことを考えれば考えるほど、頭が痛くなるばかりだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no koto o kangaereba kangaeru hodo, atama ga itaku naru bakari da.
Example (English): The more I think about him, the more my head hurts.

Grammar Point: Verb もしないで (~ mo shinai de)
Meaning: Meaning: 'without even doing'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + もしないで
Example (Japanese): 調べもしないで、答えを書きました。
Example (Romaji): Shirabe mo shinai de, kotae wo kakimashita.
Example (English): I wrote the answer without even investigating.

Grammar Point: Verb やしない (~yashinai)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'not doing such things', 'no way', or strong denial.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + やしない
Example (Japanese): こんな時に泣きやしない。
Example (Romaji): Konna toki ni nakiyashinai.
Example (English): I would never cry at a time like this.

Grammar Point: Verb よう (~ you)
Meaning: The means to do something or the way something is done.
Formation: Verb-て form + よう
Example (Japanese): この問題を解くように努力します。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wo toku you ni doryoku shimasu.
Example (English): I will try to solve this problem.

Grammar Point: Verb ようか Verbる まいか (Verb you ka Verb ru mai ka)
Meaning: Expresses hesitation or indecision between two actions; 'whether to' or 'should I or not'.
Formation: Verb-volitional + か + Verb-nonpast negative + か
Example (Japanese): 彼に話すべきようか話さぬべきか、本当に迷っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni hanasu beki you ka hanasanu beki ka, hontou ni mayotte iru.
Example (English): I'm really unsure whether I should talk to him or not.

Grammar Point: Verb ようが Verb るまいが (Verb you ga Verb ru mai ga)
Meaning: Expresses the sense of 'whether...or', 'no matter whether... or not'.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + が + Verb-negative volitional form + が
Example (Japanese): 彼が来ようが来るまいが、パーティーは始まります。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga koyou ga kurumai ga, paatii wa hajimarimasu.
Example (English): Whether he comes or not, the party will start.

Grammar Point: Verb ようがない (〜yō ga nai)
Meaning: No way to do something. Not possible.
Formation: Verb-volitional + ようがない
Example (Japanese): 電車が混んでいて、動くようがない。
Example (Romaji): Densha ga konde ite, ugoku yō ga nai.
Example (English): The train is so crowded that I can't move.

Grammar Point: Verb ようと Verbる まいと (Verb you to Verb ru mai to)
Meaning: This structure indicates that regardless if one does verb 1 or not (verb 2), the outcome remains the same.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + ようと + Verb-negative form + まいと
Example (Japanese): あなたが来ようと来るまいと、パーティーは予定通りに始まります。
Example (Romaji): Anata ga koyou to kuru mai to, paatii wa yoteidouri ni hajimarimasu.
Example (English): Whether you come or not, the party will start as scheduled.

Grammar Point: Verb ようにも (〜you ni mo)
Meaning: Used to express something that cannot be done even though one wants to.
Formation: Verb-volitional form + ようにも
Example (Japanese): もう少し速く走ろうにも、足が痛くて無理だ。
Example (Romaji): Mou sukoshi hayaku hashirou ni mo, ashi ga itakute muri da.
Example (English): I would like to run a little faster, but I can't because my leg hurts.

Grammar Point: Verb ようにも Verb れない (〜you ni mo 〜renai)
Meaning: Expresses the inability to do something even if one wants to
Formation: Verb-potential + ようにも + Verb-potential negative form
Example (Japanese): 彼を信じようにも信じられない証拠がある。
Example (Romaji): Kare o shinjiyou ni mo shinjirarenai shouko ga aru.
Example (English): There is evidence that makes it impossible to believe him, even if I want to believe him.

Grammar Point: Verb ようもない (~you mo nai)
Meaning: Expresses that something is impossible to do.
Formation: Verb-potential form-(removeい)+う + もない
Example (Japanese): この問題を解くようもない。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai o toku you mo nai.
Example (English): It's impossible to solve this problem.

Grammar Point: Verbる がままに (〜ga mama ni)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'Just as...is/does'; 'while', 'as...follows'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + がままに
Example (Japanese): 窓を開けたままに、風が部屋に入ってきました。
Example (Romaji): Mado o aketa mama ni, kaze ga heya ni haitte kimashita.
Example (English): With the window left open, the wind came into the room.

Grammar Point: Verbる が早いか (verb-ru ga hayai ka)
Meaning: Express 'as soon as' or 'the moment when'.
Formation: Verb [ます stem] + が早いか
Example (Japanese): 部屋に入るが早いか、彼はテレビをつけた。
Example (Romaji): Heya ni hairu ga hayai ka, kare wa terebi o tsuketa.
Example (English): The moment he entered the room, he turned on the TV.

Grammar Point: Verbる くらいなら (〜ru kurai nara)
Meaning: Expresses preference to avoid something; 'rather than', 'if it comes to', 'if it's as...as.'
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + くらいなら
Example (Japanese): 一人で行くくらいなら、家にいるほうがましです。
Example (Romaji): Hitori de iku kurai nara, ie ni iru hou ga mashi desu.
Example (English): I would rather stay at home than go alone.

Grammar Point: Verbる こと なし に (Verb-ru koto nashi ni)
Meaning: Used to express the meaning 'without doing'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことなしに
Example (Japanese): 試験を勉強することなしに合格しました。
Example (Romaji): Shiken wo benkyou suru koto nashi ni goukaku shimashita.
Example (English): I passed the exam without studying.

Grammar Point: Verbる ことのないように (Verb-ru koto no nai you ni)
Meaning: Expresses the desire to avoid or prevent a certain action; 'so as not to', 'to avoid'.
Formation: Verb-る + ことのないように
Example (Japanese): 車をなくすことのないように、駐車場に車をロックしましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kuruma wo nakusu koto no nai you ni, chuushajou ni kuruma wo rokku shimashou.
Example (English): In order not to lose the car, let's lock it at the parking lot.

Grammar Point: Verbる ときりがない (verb-ru to kiri ga nai)
Meaning: Used to indicate that something can go on endlessly or without limits
Formation: Verb-casual + ときりがない
Example (Japanese): 彼の悪口を言うときりがない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no waruguchi o iu to kiri ga nai.
Example (English): If we start talking about his faults, there's no end.

Grammar Point: Verbる ともなく Verb (Verb-ru tomonaku Verb)
Meaning: Used to express 'without a particular intention', 'unconsciously', 'before one knows'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ともなく + Verb
Example (Japanese): 遠くを見るともなく窓の外を眺めた。
Example (Romaji): Tooku o miru tomonaku mado no soto o nagameta.
Example (English): I found myself gazing out the window, not really looking at anything in particular.

Grammar Point: Verbる ともなしに Verb (Verb-ru tomonashi ni Verb)
Meaning: This phrase is used to express doing something unintentionally or without conscious thought.
Formation: Verb-dictionary + ともなしに + Verb
Example (Japanese): 本を読むともなしに眠ってしまった。
Example (Romaji): Hon o yomu tomonashi ni nemutte shimatta.
Example (English): I ended up falling asleep while reading the book without really meaning to.

Grammar Point: Verbる なり (Verb-ru nari)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'as soon as; the moment'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + なり
Example (Japanese): 家に帰るなり、すぐに寝た。
Example (Romaji): Ie ni kaeru nari, sugu ni neta.
Example (English): As soon as I got home, I went to bed.

Grammar Point: Verbる にとどまらず～も (Verb-ru ni todomarazu ~ mo)
Meaning: Expresses the concept of not only doing verb but also something more; 'not limited to', 'not only... but also'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + にとどまらず + extra action or outcome
Example (Japanese): 彼は仕事にとどまらず、ボランティア活動もしている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shigoto ni todomarazu, borantia katsudou mo shite iru.
Example (English): He is not only working but also doing volunteer activities.

Grammar Point: Verbる にはあたらない (Verb-ru ni wa ataranai)
Meaning: Used for saying 'it is not necessary to', 'there is no need to'.
Formation: Verbます-stem + にはあたらない
Example (Japanese): パニックに陥るにはあたらない。
Example (Romaji): Panikku ni ochiiru niwa ataranai.
Example (English): There is no need to panic.

Grammar Point: Verbる にも (Verb-ru ni mo)
Meaning: The action described by the verb is deemed impossible.
Formation: Verb-る + にも
Example (Japanese): 明日雨が降ったとしても、傘を持つことにもできない。
Example (Romaji): Ashita ame ga futta to shite mo, kasa wo motsu koto ni mo dekinai.
Example (English): Even if it rains tomorrow, I won't be able to bring an umbrella.

Grammar Point: Verbる にも Verb れない (Verbる にも Verb れない)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'even if I try or want to do something, I am still unable to do it'.
Formation: Verb-potential form + にも + Verb-negative form
Example (Japanese): 彼を理解しようにも理解できない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wo rikai shiyou ni mo rikai dekinai.
Example (English): Even if I try to understand him, I can't.

Grammar Point: Verbる べからざる Noun (Verb-ru bekara zaru Noun)
Meaning: Used to express what should not be done; 'must not', 'should not'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + べからざる + noun
Example (Japanese): 人を裏切るべからざる行為だ。
Example (Romaji): Hito o uragiru bekara zaru koui da.
Example (English): Betraying people is an act that should not be done.

Grammar Point: Verbる べからず (〜ru bekara zu)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'must not do' or 'should not do'.
Formation: Verb-ru + べからず
Example (Japanese): 嘘をつくべからず。
Example (Romaji): Uso wo tsuku bekara zu.
Example (English): One must not tell lies.

Grammar Point: Verbる べく (Verb-ru beku)
Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'in order to', 'for the purpose of'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + るべく
Example (Japanese): 成功するべく、日々努力しています。
Example (Romaji): Seikou suru beku, hibi doryoku shiteimasu.
Example (English): In order to succeed, I am working hard every day.

Grammar Point: Verbる べくもない (Verb-ru beku mo nai)
Meaning: Means 'it's impossible to...' or 'there's no way to...'
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + べくもない
Example (Japanese): その問題はとても難しく、解くべくもない。
Example (Romaji): Sono mondai wa totemo muzukashiku, toku beku mo nai.
Example (English): That problem is so difficult, it's impossible to solve.

Grammar Point: Verbる までもない (〜ru made mo nai)
Meaning: It's not necessary to the extent of; no need to.
Formation: Verb-る + までもない
Example (Japanese): そんなに心配するまでもない。
Example (Romaji): Sonna ni shinpai suru made mo nai.
Example (English): There's no need to worry that much.

Grammar Point: Verbる ものとする (〜ru mono to suru)
Meaning: Assuming or deciding something as...
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ものとする
Example (Japanese): ここでの話し合いは秘密とするものとします。
Example (Romaji): Koko de no hanashiai wa himitsu to suru mono to shimasu.
Example (English): The discussions here are to be kept confidential.

Grammar Point: Verbる や否や (verb-ru ya ina ya)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'as soon as', 'the moment'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + や否や
Example (Japanese): 彼女が家に帰るや否や、すぐにテレビをつけました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga ie ni kaeru ya ina ya, sugu ni terebi o tsukemashita.
Example (English): As soon as she returned home, she turned on the TV.

Grammar Point: Verbる 始末だ (〜ru shimatsu da)
Meaning: Expresses the result or conclusion of an action, often with a negative or unfortunate outcome.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 始末だ
Example (Japanese): 忘れてしまって、パスポートを家に置いてくる始末だった。
Example (Romaji): Wasurete shimatte, pasupooto wo ie ni okitekuru shimatsu datta.
Example (English): I ended up leaving my passport at home because I forgot.

Grammar Point: Verbる 嫌いがある (～ru kirai ga aru)
Meaning: Tendency to do a negative action; have a habit of.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 嫌いがある
Example (Japanese): 彼女は遅刻する嫌いがある。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa chikoku suru kirai ga aru.
Example (English): She has a tendency to be late.

Grammar Point: いつまで～のやら。。。 (itsumade ~ no yara)
Meaning: Express uncertainty regarding duration; 'don't know when... will end'.
Formation: いつまで + Verb-てform + のやら
Example (Japanese): この試験勉強はいつまで続くのやら。
Example (Romaji): Kono shiken benkyou wa itsumade tsuzuku no yara.
Example (English): I don't know when this exam study will end.

Grammar Point: ～が Verb られる (〜ga Verb rareru)
Meaning: Expresses potential or ability to do something; 'can', 'able to'.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + られる
Example (Japanese): 彼がこの問題を解けると思いますか？
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kono mondai o tokeru to omoimasu ka?
Example (English): Do you think he can solve this problem?

Grammar Point: ～かと思いきや (〜ka to omoikiya)
Meaning: Expressing unexpected outcomes; 'just when I thought', 'but'.
Formation: Sentence + かと思いきや, (Noun/ な-Adjective + だ/ い-Adjective/ Verb (past form) + かと思いきや)
Example (Japanese): 明日は晴れるかと思いきや、まさかの雨が降った。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa hareru ka to omoikiya, masaka no ame ga futta.
Example (English): I thought it would be sunny tomorrow, but unexpectedly it rained.

Grammar Point: ～がゆえに (～ga yue ni)
Meaning: Expresses the reason or cause; 'because', 'due to', 'as a result of'.
Formation: Noun + がゆえに
Example (Japanese): 愛情がゆえに、彼は彼女を許した。
Example (Romaji): Aijou ga yue ni, kare wa kanojo o yurushita.
Example (English): Because of love, he forgave her.

Grammar Point: ～がゆえの Noun (〜ga yue no Noun)
Meaning: Expresses the reason or cause for something; 'because of', 'due to'.
Formation: Noun / Verb-dictionary form + がゆえの + Noun
Example (Japanese): 愛がゆえの悲しみ。
Example (Romaji): Ai ga yue no kanashimi.
Example (English): Sadness due to love.

Grammar Point: ～から Noun に 至る まで (〜kara 〜ni itaru made)
Meaning: Expressing range from one thing to another; 'from...to', 'ranging from...to'.
Formation: Noun[始点] + から + Noun[終点] + に至るまで
Example (Japanese): このバンドの曲は、青年から老人に至るまで、人々に愛されています。
Example (Romaji): Kono bando no kyoku wa, seinen kara roujin ni itaru made, hitobito ni aisarete imasu.
Example (English): The songs of this band are loved by people, ranging from young to old.

Grammar Point: ～ごとく (〜gotoku)
Meaning: To seem like; as if; as though.
Formation: Verb-て + ごとく,  Noun + の + ごとく
Example (Japanese): 彼は鳥のごとく飛んでいるように見えた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa tori no gotoku tonde iru you ni mieta.
Example (English): He looked as though he was flying like a bird.

Grammar Point: ～こととて (〜koto tote)
Meaning: Used to express the reason or premise for a decision or judgement; 'since', 'because'.
Formation: Verb-casual + こととて, Noun + の + こととて
Example (Japanese): 彼は裁判を勝つために全資産を使うこととて、弁護士に頼んだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa saiban o katsu tame ni zenshisan o tsukau koto tote, bengoshi ni tanonda.
Example (English): Since he is using all his assets to win the trial, he asked a lawyer.

Grammar Point: ～ずにすんだ (〜zuni sunda)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'was able to do without'; 'managed to avoid'.
Formation: Verb-ず form + に + すんだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は事故を起こさずにすんだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa jiko o okosazu ni sunda.
Example (English): He managed to avoid having an accident.

Grammar Point: ～だろうとなかろうと (〜darou to nakarou to)
Meaning: Expresses 'regardless of whether it is or isn't'.
Formation: Noun + だろうとなかろうと
Example (Japanese): 試験が難しいだろうとなかろうと、全力で頑張ります。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga muzukashii darou to nakarou to, zenryoku de ganbarimasu.
Example (English): Regardless of whether the exam is difficult or not, I will do my best.

Grammar Point: ～つもりだ (〜tsumori da)
Meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + つもりだ
Example (Japanese): 明日は早く起きるつもりです。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa hayaku okiru tsumori desu.
Example (English): I plan to wake up early tomorrow.

Grammar Point: ～つもりで (〜tsumori de)
Meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan; 'with the intention of', 'planning to'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + つもりで
Example (Japanese): 私は日本に住むつもりで日本語を勉強しています。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa Nihon ni sumu tsumori de Nihongo o benkyou shiteimasu.
Example (English): I am studying Japanese with the intention of living in Japan.

Grammar Point: ～ではすまない (〜dewa sumanai)
Meaning: Expresses the speaker's strong feeling that just doing something is not enough or will not suffice.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ではすまない, い-adjective + ではすまない, な-adjective + ではすまない, Noun + ではすまない
Example (Japanese): ただ謝るではすまない。何か行動を取らなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Tada ayamaru dewa sumanai. Nanika koudou o toranakereba naranai.
Example (English): Just apologizing will not suffice. Some action needs to be taken.

Grammar Point: ～とあって (〜to atte)
Meaning: Expresses a special situation or event due to certain circumstances.
Formation: Noun + とあって
Example (Japanese): 春休みとあって、公園は子供たちでいっぱいだ。
Example (Romaji): Haruyasumi to atte, kouen wa kodomo-tachi de ippai da.
Example (English): Because it's spring break, the park is full of children.

Grammar Point: ～とあれば (〜to areba)
Meaning: Express a condition; 'if', 'when', 'since'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とあれば, い-Adjective + とあれば,な-Adjective + だとあれば, Noun + だとあれば
Example (Japanese): 無料とあれば、誰でも利用したいと思います。
Example (Romaji): Muryou to areba, dare demo riyou shitai to omoimasu.
Example (English): If it's free, everyone would want to use it.

Grammar Point: ～といえども (〜to iedomo)
Meaning: Even if it is said that; Even though; Although
Formation: Noun + といえども, Verb-plain form + といえども
Example (Japanese): 彼が天才といえども、ミスをすることはあります。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga tensai to iedomo, misu o suru koto wa arimasu.
Example (English): Even though he is a genius, he makes mistakes.

Grammar Point: ～といったらありはしない (〜to ittara ari wa shinai)
Meaning: Express extreme exclamation; 'extremely', 'unbelievable', 'unsurpassed'.
Formation: Noun + といったらありはしない, な-Adjective + といったらありはしない
Example (Japanese): 彼の英語の上手さといったらありはしない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no eigo no jouzusa to ittara ari wa shinai.
Example (English): His English is unbelievably good.

Grammar Point: ～といったらありゃしない (〜to ittara arya shinai)
Meaning: Used to emphasise that something is to the extreme; 'you have no idea how...', 'it's incredibly...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + といったらありゃしない, い-Adjective + といったらありゃしない, な-Adjective + だといったらありゃしない, Noun + だといったらありゃしない
Example (Japanese): その店のラーメンは美味しいといったらありゃしない。
Example (Romaji): Sono mise no ramen wa oishii to ittara arya shinai.
Example (English): You have no idea how delicious the ramen at that shop is.

Grammar Point: ～といったらない。 (〜to ittara nai)
Meaning: Expresses the extreme of something; 'nothing can be more ... than this'
Formation: i-Adjective + といったらない, な-Adjective + だといったらない, Noun + だといったらない
Example (Japanese): 今日は寒いといったらない。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa samui to ittara nai.
Example (English): It's extremely cold today.

Grammar Point: ～ときている (〜to kite iru)
Meaning: Used to express that a situation is serious or extreme, often with a negative connotation.
Formation: Verb-casual, い-Adjective, な-Adjective +で + ときている, Noun + だ + ときている
Example (Japanese): 仕事が忙しいときているから、オフィスでは集中できない。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto ga isogashii toki te iru kara, ofisu de wa shuuchuu dekinai.
Example (English): With how busy work is, I can't concentrate in the office.

Grammar Point: ～ところを (〜tokoro wo)
Meaning: Expresses the concept of 'despite' or 'even though'.
Formation: Verb-てform + いる + ところを, Noun + の + ところを, い-Adjective + ところを, な-Adjective + な + ところを
Example (Japanese): 見ているところを、急に停電になった。
Example (Romaji): Mite iru tokoro wo, kyuu ni teiden ni natta.
Example (English): Even though I was watching, it suddenly blacked out.

Grammar Point: ～とされる (〜to sareru)
Meaning: Indicates a general belief or widely accepted view; often translated as 'is considered', 'is seen as', 'is said to be'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とされる, い-Adjective + とされる, な-Adjective + だとされる, Noun + だとされる
Example (Japanese): サッカーは世界で最も人気のあるスポーツとされています。
Example (Romaji): Sakkaa wa sekai de motto mo ninki no aru supootsu to sareteimasu.
Example (English): Soccer is considered the most popular sport in the world.

Grammar Point: ～としたところで (〜to shita tokoro de)
Meaning: Even if; even though; even assuming
Formation: Verb-casual + としたところで, い-Adjective + としたところで,な-Adjective + だとしたところで, Noun + だとしたところで
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るとしたところで、何も変わらないだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru to shita tokoro de, nani mo kawaranai darou.
Example (English): Even if he comes, nothing will probably change.

Grammar Point: ～とすると (〜to suru to)
Meaning: Expresses 'when', 'if', 'given that' in a speculative or hypothetical sense.
Formation: Verb-casual + とすると, い-Adjective + とすると,な-Adjective + だとすると, Noun + だとすると
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るとすると、もうすぐここに着くはずです。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru to suru to, mou sugu koko ni tsuku hazu desu.
Example (English): If he is coming, he should arrive here soon.

Grammar Point: ～とすれば (～to sureba)
Meaning: Used to express 'if it were the case', 'if we assume'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とすれば, い-Adjective + とすれば, な-Adjective + だとすれば, Noun + だとすれば
Example (Japanese): 彼が嘘つきだとすれば、その話は信じられない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga usotsuki da to sureba, sono hanashi wa shinjirarenai.
Example (English): If he's a liar, then his story can't be believed.

Grammar Point: ～となったら (〜to nattara)
Meaning: Used to express 'when', 'if it comes to', 'in the case of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + となったら, Noun + となったら
Example (Japanese): 旅行に行くとなったら、荷造りをしなくてはなりません。
Example (Romaji): Ryokou ni iku to nattara, nizouri o shinakute wa narimasen.
Example (English): If it comes to going on a trip, we have to pack.

Grammar Point: ～となると (〜to naru to)
Meaning: Used to highlight a certain circumstance or condition; 'when it comes to', 'if it becomes', 'in the case of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + となると, い-Adjective + となると,な-Adjective + だとなると, Noun + だとなると
Example (Japanese): 試験となると、多くの学生が緊張します。
Example (Romaji): Shiken to naru to, ōku no gakusei ga kinchō shimasu.
Example (English): When it comes to exams, many students become nervous.

Grammar Point: ～となれば (〜to nareba)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'if it comes to...; when we talk about...; in the case of...'.
Formation: Verb-casual + となれば, い-Adjective + となれば,な-Adjective + だとなれば, Noun + だとなれば
Example (Japanese): 彼がリーダーとなれば、プロジェクトは成功するでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga riidaa to nareba, purojekuto wa seikou suru deshou.
Example (English): If he becomes the leader, the project will probably succeed.

Grammar Point: ～とのことだ (〜to no koto da)
Meaning: Expresses something that the speaker heard; 'I've heard that', 'I was told that'.
Formation: Simplified phrase + とのことだ
Example (Japanese): 週末にパーティーがあるとのことだ。
Example (Romaji): Shuumatsu ni paatii ga aru to no koto da.
Example (English): I've heard that there is a party this weekend.

Grammar Point: ～とはいえ (～to wa ie)
Meaning: Even though; although; but
Formation: Noun + とはいえ, な-Adjective + だとはいえ, い-Adjective + とはいえ, Verb-casual + とはいえ
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭が良いとはいえ、少し怠け者だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga yoi to wa ie, sukoshi namakemono da.
Example (English): Although he is smart, he is a bit lazy.

Grammar Point: ～とみえて (〜to miete)
Meaning: It seems that; apparently
Formation: Verb-casual + とみえて, い-Adjective + とみえて,な-Adjective + だとみえて, Noun + だとみえて
Example (Japanese): 彼は運動が得意とみえて、毎日ジムに行っています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa undou ga tokui to miete, mainichi jimu ni itteimasu.
Example (English): He seems to be good at exercise, as he goes to the gym every day.

Grammar Point: ～とみられる (～to mirareru)
Meaning: It is considered that; It is thought that; It is believed that
Formation: Verb-casual+ とみられる, Noun + とみられる
Example (Japanese): 彼の行動は無責任とみられる。
Example (Romaji): Kare no koudou wa musekinin to mirareru.
Example (English): His behavior is considered irresponsible.

Grammar Point: ～とみると (〜to miru to)
Meaning: Expresses the concept of 'when one sees it as', 'viewed as', or 'considering'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とみると, い-Adjective + とみると, な-Adjective + だとみると, Noun + だとみると
Example (Japanese): この問題を数学の視点でとみると、解決策が見えてきます。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai o suugaku no shiten de to miru to, kaiketsusaku ga miete kimasu.
Example (English): When one sees this problem from a mathematical perspective, a solution begins to emerge.

Grammar Point: どんなに～うが (donna ni ～ u ga)
Meaning: Expresses 'no matter how much...', 'even if...'.
Formation: どんなに + Verb-casual + うが, どんなに + い-Adjective + うが, どんなに + な-Adjective + だろうが
Example (Japanese): どんなに頑張ったうが、彼の速さには追いつけない。
Example (Romaji): Donna ni ganbatta u ga, kare no hayasa ni ha oitsukenai.
Example (English): No matter how hard I try, I can't catch up with his speed.

Grammar Point: ～と言わんばかりに (〜to iwan bakari ni)
Meaning: Indicates an action or behavior that strongly implies a certain unspoken message or feeling.
Formation: Verb-volitional + と言わんばかりに, い-Adjective + と言わんばかりに, な-Adjective + だと言わんばかりに, Noun + だと言わんばかりに
Example (Japanese): 彼女は優勝したと言わんばかりに笑った。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa yuushou shita to iwanbakari ni waratta.
Example (English): She laughed as if to say she won.

Grammar Point: ～と言わんばかりの Noun (～to iwan bakari no Noun)
Meaning: Expresses the concept of 'as if to say'; 'almost says'; 'suggests'.
Formation: Verb-plain form + と言わんばかりの Noun
Example (Japanese): 田中さんは嬉しくて飛び上がると言わんばかりの笑顔を見せた。
Example (Romaji): Tanaka-san wa ureshikute tobiagaru to iwan bakari no egao wo miseta.
Example (English): Tanaka showed a smile as if to say he was so happy he could jump for joy.

Grammar Point: ～ながらに (～nagara ni)
Meaning: Expresses the meaning 'while', 'as', or 'since'.
Formation: Noun + ながらに, な-Adjective (without 'na') + ながらに
Example (Japanese): 彼は若いながらにすごく経験豊富です。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa wakai nagara ni sugoku keikenhoufu desu.
Example (English): Even though he is young, he is very experienced.

Grammar Point: ～ながらの Noun (〜nagara no Noun)
Meaning: This grammar point is used to indicate that two actions are happening simultaneously.
Formation: Verb-てform + ながらの + Noun
Example (Japanese): テレビを見ながらの夕食は、子供たちにとって楽しいだろう。
Example (Romaji): Terebi wo minagara no yuushoku wa, kodomotachi ni totte tanoshii darou.
Example (English): Dinner while watching TV might be fun for the children.

Grammar Point: ～ながらも (〜nagara mo)
Meaning: Despite doing something or 'even though'.
Formation: Verb-ながらも
Example (Japanese): 彼は貧しいながらも、幸せな生活を送っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mazushii nagaramo, shiawase na seikatsu wo okutte iru.
Example (English): Despite being poor, he leads a happy life.

Grammar Point: ～なくはない (〜naku wa nai)
Meaning: Used to express the idea that 'it's not that it's not', implying something is possible but not certain.
Formation: Verb-ないform + なくはない, い-Adjective－い ＋ くはない, な-Adjective + ではなくはない, Noun + ではなくはない
Example (Japanese): それを終えるのは難しくなくはない。
Example (Romaji): Sore wo oeru no wa muzukashikunaku wa nai.
Example (English): It's not that it's impossible to finish it.

Grammar Point: ～なくもない (〜naku mo nai)
Meaning: Express the possibility; 'not impossible', 'might as well'.
Formation: Verb-ないform + もない, い-Adjective-removeい + くもない, な-Adjective + でもない, Noun + でもない
Example (Japanese): 彼がもうすぐ戻るなら、待つなくもない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga mou sugu modoru nara, matsu naku mo nai.
Example (English): If he will be back soon, it wouldn't be a bad idea to wait.

Grammar Point: ～なら～なりに
Meaning: This grammar point means 'if it is X, it is X in its own way', emphasizing the characteristics of X.
Formation: Noun + なら(そのN)なりに/Adjective + なら(その adj.)なりに
Example (Japanese): 彼はまだ初心者なら初心者なりに頑張っている。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mada shoshinsha nara shoshinsha nari ni ganbatteiru.
Example (English): If he is still a beginner, he is working hard in his own way as a beginner.

Grammar Point: ～には及ばない (〜ni wa oyobanai)
Meaning: Not necessary; Unworthy of
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + には及ばない
Example (Japanese): ファーストクラスに乗るには及ばない、エコノミークラスでも十分だ。
Example (Romaji): Fāsuto kurasu ni noru ni wa oyobanai, ekonomī kurasu demo juubun da.
Example (English): There is no need to go as far as to ride in first class, economy class is enough.

Grammar Point: ～に堪えない (～ni taenai)
Meaning: Used to express that something is unbearable or hard to stand.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + に堪えない, Noun + に堪えない
Example (Japanese): この暑さはもう耐えられない。
Example (Romaji): Kono atsusa wa mou taerarenai.
Example (English): I can't stand this heat anymore.

Grammar Point: ～に堪える (～ni taeru)
Meaning: Signify 'cannot stand', 'can’t help but feel', 'cannot be overlooked'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + に堪える, Verb-nai form + に堪える, い-adjective + さ + に堪える, な-Adjective + さ + に堪える, Noun + の + に堪える
Example (Japanese): この暑さはもう我慢に堪えない。
Example (Romaji): Kono atsusa wa mou gaman ni taenai.
Example (English): I can't stand this heat anymore.

Grammar Point: ～に耐える (～ni taeru)
Meaning: To endure or withstand something; 'endure', 'withstand', 'tolerate'.
Formation: Noun + に耐える
Example (Japanese): 彼は厳しい修行に耐えた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kibishii shugyou ni taeta.
Example (English): He endured the harsh training.

Grammar Point: ～に至った (〜ni itatta)
Meaning: Expresses the outcome of a process or a series of events; 'reached the point', 'led to'.
Formation: Verb-てform + に至った
Example (Japanese): 彼は練習を重ねて、ついにプロのギタリストに至った。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa renshuu o kasanete, tsui ni puro no gitarisuto ni itatta.
Example (English): After repeated practice, he finally became a professional guitarist.

Grammar Point: ～に越したことはない (〜ni koshita koto wa nai)
Meaning: Expresses the idea 'it is best to...' or 'nothing better than...'.
Formation: Verb-てform + に越したことはない, い-Adjective + に越したことはない,な-Adjective + に越したことはない, Noun + に越したことはない
Example (Japanese): 早く準備するに越したことはない。
Example (Romaji): Hayaku junbi suru ni koshita koto wa nai.
Example (English): It is best to prepare early.

Grammar Point: ～に難くない (～ni muzukunai)
Meaning: Expresses the idea that something is not difficult; 'not difficult to ~'
Formation: Verb-ない form (Remove ない) + に難くない
Example (Japanese): この手紙を読むのに難くない。
Example (Romaji): Kono tegami wo yomu no ni muzukunai.
Example (English): It's not difficult to read this letter.

Grammar Point: ～のは Noun ぐらいのものだ (〜no wa 〜 gurai no mono da)
Meaning: Expresses the idea that 'only/exclusively Noun' or 'nothing but Noun'.
Formation: Verb-casual + のは Noun + ぐらいのものだ, い-Adjective + のは Noun + ぐらいのものだ,な-Adjective + のは Noun + ぐらいのものだ, Noun + のは Noun + ぐらいのものだ
Example (Japanese): この小説を読むのは楽しみぐらいのものだ。
Example (Romaji): Kono shousetsu wo yomu no wa tanoshimi gurai no mono da.
Example (English): The only thing about reading this novel is pleasure.

Grammar Point: ～ば～ものを (～ba～mono o)
