Meaning: Expresses regret about a situation that did not happen; 'if only', 'it would be good if'.
Formation: Verb-casual, past + ば + Verb-casual, past + ものを, い-Adjective + ければ + い-Adjective + ものを, な-Adjective + であれば + な-Adjective + ものを, Noun + であれば + Noun + ものを
Example (Japanese): 早く起きれば、遅刻しなかったものを。
Example (Romaji): Hayaku okireba, chikoku shinakatta mono o.
Example (English): If only I had woken up early, I would not have been late.

Grammar Point: ～びた Noun (～ bi ta ～)
Meaning: Used to emphasise the objective or target of an action.
Formation: Verb-volitional + びた + Noun
Example (Japanese): とっつきびた友人になりたい。
Example (Romaji): Tottsukibi ta tomodachi ni naritai.
Example (English): I want to become a lifelong friend.

Grammar Point: ～びる (〜biru)
Meaning: Express an action that one does repeatedly or habitually.
Formation: Verbs-masu-stem + びる
Example (Japanese): 彼は毎日のようにジョギングに行きびる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mainichi no you ni jogingu ni iki biru.
Example (English): He goes jogging almost every day.

Grammar Point: ～ぶった
Meaning: This structure is used to indicate something 'struck with' or 'hit by' the meaning of the noun.
Formation: Noun + を + ぶった, Verb +て/で + ぶった
Example (Japanese): 彼は突然失業をぶった。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa totsuzen shitsugyou wo butta.
Example (English): He was suddenly hit by unemployment.

Grammar Point: ～ぶって (〜butte)
Meaning: Used to express the act of pretending or acting in a particular manner.
Formation: Verb-stem + ぶって
Example (Japanese): 彼はまるで知っているふうにぶって話を進めていた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa marude shitteiru fuu ni butte hanashi o susumete ita.
Example (English): He was talking as if he knew everything.

Grammar Point: ～ぶり (〜buri)
Meaning: Express the amount of time elapsed since doing something last.
Formation: Time expression + ぶり
Example (Japanese): 三年ぶりに彼に会いました。
Example (Romaji): San-nen buri ni kare ni aimashita.
Example (English): I met him for the first time in three years.

Grammar Point: ～ぶる (〜buru)
Meaning: Used when someone is acting or pretending to be something they are not.
Formation: Noun + ぶる
Example (Japanese): 彼はあたかも知っているかのように学者ぶる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atakamo shitte iru ka no you ni gakusha buru.
Example (English): He acts like a scholar as if he knows everything.

Grammar Point: ～までだ (～made da)
Meaning: Expresses the limit or 'up to' something; 'it's only', 'as far as', 'up to'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form or ない form + までだ, い-Adjective + までだ, Noun + までだ
Example (Japanese): 彼とは友達までだ、それ以上の関係ではありません。
Example (Romaji): Kare to wa tomodachi made da, sore ijou no kankei dewa arimasen.
Example (English): With him, it's only up to friendship, there's no more relationship than that.

Grammar Point: ～もなんでもない (〜mo nandemonai)
Meaning: Expression used to dismiss or negate something's importance or significance; 'it's nothing at all', 'it does not matter'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + もなんでもない, い-Adjective + もなんでもない,な-Adjective + なもなんでもない, Noun + もなんでもない
Example (Japanese): 100万円を負けるもなんでもない。
Example (Romaji): Hyaku man en o makeru mo nandemonai.
Example (English): Losing a million yen is nothing at all.

Grammar Point: ～ものとして (～mono to shite)
Meaning: Assuming/Under the assumption that/In the event.
Formation: Verb-casual + ものとして, い-Adjective + ものとして, な-Adjective + なものとして, Noun + のものとして
Example (Japanese): 雨が降るものとして、傘を持って行きました。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga furu mono to shite, kasa wo motte ikimashita.
Example (English): Assuming that it would rain, I brought an umbrella.

Grammar Point: ～んがために (〜n ga tame ni)
Meaning: Expresses the reason or purpose for doing something; 'for the sake of', 'in order to'.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + んがために, Noun + のんがために
Example (Japanese): 健康を保つんがために、毎日運動をしています。
Example (Romaji): Kenkou o tamotsu n ga tame ni, mainichi undou o shite imasu.
Example (English): I exercise daily in order to maintain my health.

Grammar Point: ～んばかりに (〜n bakari ni ～)
Meaning: Expresses the idea of 'as if to say' or 'as though' something is the case.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + んばかりに, Noun + ばかりに
Example (Japanese): 彼は、何も知らないんばかりに、私の質問を無視した。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa, nani mo shiranai n bakari ni, watashi no shitsumon o mushi shita.
Example (English): He ignored my question as if he knew nothing.

Grammar Point: ～差し支えない (〜sashi tsukaenai)
Meaning: Expresses the lack of a problem or obstacle; 'it's not a problem', 'it doesn't matter', 'there's no harm'.
Formation: Verb-てform + も差し支えない, Noun + が差し支えない
Example (Japanese): 多少遅くても差し支えないです。
Example (Romaji): Tashou osokutemo sashitsukaenai desu.
Example (English): It's not a problem even if it's a little late.

Grammar Point: ～折に (〜ori ni)
Meaning: Indicates the time when something happens; 'when', 'at the time of'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 折に, Noun + の折に
Example (Japanese): 父が病気の折に、私は留学していました。
Example (Romaji): Chichi ga byouki no ori ni, watashi wa ryuugaku shite imashita.
Example (English): When my father was ill, I was studying abroad.

Grammar Point: ～極まりない (〜kiwamarinai)
Meaning: Express extreme state; 'extremely', 'utterly', 'to the utmost'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 極まりない, Noun + の極まりない
Example (Japanese): この試験の難しさは極まりない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shiken no muzukashisa wa kiwamarinai.
Example (English): The difficulty of this test is extreme.

Grammar Point: ～極まる (〜kiwamaru)
Meaning: Expresses the idea 'to the utmost', or 'to the extreme'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 極まる/極まりない, い-Adjective remove い + 極まる/極まりない,な-Adjective + 極まる/極まりない, Noun + 極まる/極まりない
Example (Japanese): 彼の無礼さは極まる。
Example (Romaji): Kare no bureisa wa kiwamaru.
Example (English): His rudeness is to the extreme.

Grammar Point: ～足りない (～tarinai)
Meaning: Express insufficiency or lack of something.
Formation: Verb-casual, non-past + ほど/だけ + 足りない, Noun + が + 足りない
Example (Japanese): 私の日本語の能力はまだまだ足りない。
Example (Romaji): Watashi no nihongo no nouryoku wa madamada tarinai.
Example (English): My Japanese ability is still not enough.

Grammar Point: ～足る Noun (〜taru～)
Meaning: Express that something is sufficient; 'enough', 'sufficient'.
Formation: Noun + 足る
Example (Japanese): この料理は4人分足る。
Example (Romaji): Kono ryouri wa yoninbun taru.
Example (English): This dish is enough for four people.

Grammar Point: ～限りだ (〜kagiri da)
Meaning: Expresses an extreme state or condition; translated as 'to the utmost', 'extremely', 'as can be'.
Formation: Verb-casual, past + 限りだ, い-Adjective + 限りだ
Example (Japanese): 彼女が結婚してしまった。驚きの限りだ。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga kekkon shite shimatta. Odoroki no kagiri da.
Example (English): She got married. I'm as shocked as can be.
